question: How many people must be in a room for an even chance that two birthdays fall within a day of each other?
answer: About 14. Each person now blocks three days of the calendar rather than one, so near-clashes pile up far faster than exact ones. Diaconis and Mosteller set out the general rule in 1989. Allow a week either side and seven people suffice: one dinner table.
move: Every nearly you allow multiplies the ways a coincidence can happen.
ask: What coincidence in my life would feel ordinary if I counted all the chances it had?
trap: Reaching for 23, the famous figure for exactly shared birthdays.
